verdicts.observation_being_explained: numeric-coverage-001: probes collected output IDs and CHOSEN logprobs but raw top_logprobs was null for reference and candidate
verdicts.completions_quirk: /v1/completions ignores the standard OpenAI `top_logprobs` field entirely; its `logprobs` field is typed Optional[int] (protocol.py:377) and doubles as the k count (serving_completions.py:120). A standard-shape {logprobs:true, top_logprobs:20} request silently yields k=1.
verdicts.engine_bug: NONE FOUND on the chat/native paths: with the top-k field set, sampler + logprob_result_processor + tokenizer_manager all consume top_logprobs_num (guards at logprob_result_processor.py:60/92/256/268; tokenizer_manager.py:1590-1591). The null is the engine correctly reporting that no top-k was requested.

recommended_probe_recipe.raw_evidence_variant: add return_flat_raw_output_top_logprobs=true (+ optionally return_flat_raw_top_logprobs_b64=true): flat raw arrays of top-k values + token ids, no detokenized strings; single-item requests only, not with stream=true (io_struct.py:250-254, 457-476)
recommended_probe_recipe.uncertainty: no engine-side cap on top_logprobs_num was found by grep; k=20 chosen to match the OpenAI-style ceiling. If a cap exists elsewhere the populated(k=...) result would show it immediately on re-run.
